paper_metadata.title: Factors affecting one year mortality and functional outcome after first ever ischemic stroke in the region of Antalya, Turkey (A Hospital-based study)

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study describes the source population and recruitment period well. However, it is a hospital-based study in a single center, which the authors admit may not represent the general population (selection bias). The participation rate of eligible individuals is not explicitly stated, though they mention 'consecutive' recruitment.

items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the geographic and clinical source of the patients.

items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment from a specific department is a standard method to reduce selection bias in hospital-based studies.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a high rate of loss to follow-up (26.8%), and the authors do not provide a comparison of baseline characteristics between those who completed the study and those lost to follow-up. This creates a high risk of attrition bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcomes (mortality and functional status) are well-defined. The use of the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) is a validated approach, and the same physician performed the assessments, reducing inter-rater variability.

items.evidence_snippet: Functional disability was measured by the modified Rankin scale which was applied on the day of attendance and at the end of one year by the same physician
items.reasoning: The mRS is a validated tool. Having the same physician perform assessments ensures consistency, though blinding to prognostic factors is not mentioned.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for many clinical and socioeconomic confounders in a multivariable model. However, the authors acknowledge the lack of data on the cause of death and cognitive/psychological deficits, which are important potential confounders in stroke prognosis.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Demographic and socioeconomic variables, stroke risk factors, stroke subtype and neurological findings were noted.
items.reasoning: While many factors were measured, the authors admit they did not evaluate cognitive and psychological deficits, nor did they record specific treatments received during the year.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: History of hypertension was defined as documented treatment of hypertension or systolic blood pressure > 140 mm Hg... Diabetes mellitus was defined as usage of blood sugar lowering drugs...
items.reasoning: The authors provide specific clinical thresholds for the confounders/risk factors measured.

items.evidence_snippet: Atrial fibrilation was diagnosed by ECG ... Hypercholesterolaemia was considered if one plasma cholesterol value was 240 mg/dl or higher
items.reasoning: Confounders were measured using standard diagnostic tests (ECG, blood tests).

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that only illiteracy, being single or widowed and presence of urinary incontinence were significant predictors
items.reasoning: The authors used multivariable logistic regression to adjust for variables that were significant in univariate analysis.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are generally appropriate, but the small sample size (n=147) and the high number of variables (19) entered into the analysis may lead to overfitting of the logistic regression model. Additionally, the high attrition rate is not addressed in the analysis (e.g., sensitivity analysis).

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Continuous data were analysed using the independent samples t tests, categorical data using the chi-square tests. Independent variables which were significant at the 0.05 level were entered into the multivariate logistic regression analysis.
items.reasoning: The analytical steps are clearly laid out.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Independent variables which were significant at the 0.05 level were entered into the multivariate logistic regression analysis.
items.reasoning: The study uses a p-value-driven approach for variable selection rather than a purely conceptual framework, which can be prone to bias, especially with small samples.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariate logistic regression analysis ... Associations were presented as hazard ratios with their corresponding 95% confidence interval
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for the dichotomous outcomes (dead/alive, dependent/independent).
